We need to produce JSON route with type mol root, children reaction nodes etc. Need to select appropriate templates. We can search for templates matching functional group transformations: likely steps: 1) SN2 to attach side chain? The target has a side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to N of triazine? Actually structure: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. Contains anisole ring with amide linking to a triazine (c2nnn...). The triazine has a substituent Cc3... (benzyl attached to heterocycle). That benzyl has a side chain CN4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-member? It's N4CC(F)C4: a morpholine? It's a N-azetidine with fluorine. So we need retrosynthesis: break amide (retro amide formation via condensation of amine and acid). Break C-N bond between benzyl and triazine (maybe SN2). Break Friedel-Crafts acylation to form anisole ring? Actually anisole ring attached to amide; could be formed via Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from triazine carboxylic acid? The forward reaction: Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl group to aromatic ring, breaking halide (acyl chloride). So retro: remove acyl group to give anisole and acyl chloride (or acid). So step1: retrosynthetic disconnection of amide: target -> anisole (COc1cccc(NH) c1?) Actually anisole with amine? The amide bond between anisole amine (anilide) and carbonyl attached to triazine. So retro: break amide to give aniline (COc1cccc(NH2?) Actually the aniline would be COc1cccc(NH2) c1) and carboxylic acid derivative of triazine (c2nnn(... )c2N-COOH). That could be formed via Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from that acid. So step2: the triazine acid could be formed via SN2 attaching benzyl group? Actually the triazine has substituent Cc3... which is a benzyl attached to triazine nitrogen (N-alkylation). That could be formed via SN2 of triazine nitrogen with benzyl halide. So retro: break N-CH2 bond to give triazine with NH (instead of N-CH2-aryl) and benzyl halide (e.g., benzyl chloride). Then benzyl chloride could be formed via substitution of benzyl alcohol with halogen (e.g., using thionyl chloride). That's third step: convert benzyl alcohol to benzyl chloride.

Thus 3 reactions: 1) amide formation (retro: amide cleavage) using template for amide bond formation (functional groups broken: amide). 2) N-alkylation SN2 (retro: break C-N bond) using SN2 template. 3) substitution of alcohol to halide (retro: convert halide to alcohol). Provide template IDs? We need to search template catalog. Let's search for SN2 template.
